WITH joined_data AS (
  SELECT 
    sf.instownpct,
    tr.ordertypedist
  FROM sentimentandfundamentals sf
  INNER JOIN transactionrecord tr ON sf.transref = tr.transreg
  WHERE tr.ordertypedist IS NOT NULL
    AND sf.instownpct IS NOT NULL
),
overall_avg_value AS (
  SELECT AVG(instownpct) as overall_avg
  FROM joined_data
),
type_averages AS (
  SELECT 
    ordertypedist,
    AVG(instownpct) as type_avg
  FROM joined_data
  GROUP BY ordertypedist
),
above_average_cases AS (
  SELECT 
    jd.instownpct,
    jd.ordertypedist,
    oav.overall_avg,
    ta.type_avg
  FROM joined_data jd
  CROSS JOIN overall_avg_value oav
  JOIN type_averages ta ON jd.ordertypedist = ta.ordertypedist
  WHERE jd.instownpct > oav.overall_avg
)
SELECT 
  AVG(instownpct) as avg_ownership,
  AVG(instownpct / type_avg) as avg_ownership_ratio,
  AVG(instownpct - overall_avg) as avg_excess
FROM above_average_cases;

assumptions.assumption: The "average ratio of their ownership to the average ownership for their order type mix" is computed as the mean of individual ratios (each case's instownpct divided by the average instownpct for its order type), not as the ratio of aggregate averages.

alternatives.interpretation: The second metric could separately group above-average cases by order type, compute each group's average ownership relative to its type average, then average those group-level ratios across order types.
